correctness.rationale: For positive C1 strictly decreasing log-concave input, the filtered ratio \(U/f\) strictly increases by monotone fractional hazard. \((e^{rt}D')'=e^{rt}f'<0\) establishes uniqueness of a peak on each constant-rate reach and treats equality. One interface produces a derivative jump \((b-c)U(d)>0\). Positive-solution comparison as interface moves yields a strictly decreasing downstream peak height; its values straddle the fixed upstream peak, giving one global-worst-site crossover. The exponential example and the strict bracket 1.091575--1.091576 were checked with exact rational remainder enclosures in verify.py; randomized computations are supplementary and not a substitute for proof.

value.rationale: The number of oxygen minima is not determined by the number of pollutant sources in a reach-heterogeneous river. The theorem proves an exact, hazard-general two-sag window and a unique switch in which site gives worst modeled oxygen deficit even when two local minima persist at every sufficiently late interface. This is a natural interpretation/monitoring benchmark for locally varying reaeration and is neither a textbook fixed-reach sag calculation nor a numerical grid observation. Its simplified assumptions and lack of field calibration are stated.
